transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I guess my wife wanted me to come in. It's just... I can't really stop thinking about how rough my face and hands look. I mean, I know I've worked outside my whole life, but... it's the cracks and the spots. The sagging. It's all I can see. Whenever I have to go into town, like to the bank or the county office, I just know they're all staring at it. My wife says I just look like a man who's worked outdoors, but... I don't know. It just bothers me a lot.
Are you worried about anything else besides how your face and hands look?
No, not really. Just... just what I said. My face and hands. That's about it.
Has this concern about your face and hands affected your daily life or relationships in any way?

Well... I suppose it has a bit. I've, uh... I've missed a couple of meetings with the bankers lately. Just put off some farm decisions because... I don't know, I just couldn't get myself looking acceptable enough to sit down in a room with folks. 

And my wife, she's been trying to get pictures to promote our farm retreat and the craft sales we do, but... I told her to stop asking. I just won't agree to be in any photos for that anymore. That's... that's about it, really.
Have your concerns about your face and hands been constant, or do they come and go?
I don't really know... I haven't kept track of it like that. I guess it's just... on my mind most days. I couldn't rightly say if it comes and goes, it's just... something I notice.
Is it the overall appearance of your face and hands that bothers you, or is there something specific about them that you're concerned with?

I suppose... it's specific things. Just how rough and worn they look. The, uh... the cracks in my hands. The spots and the sagging on my face. I just can't seem to get past it. 

It feels like every banker or county person I sit down with is just staring right at all those spots and cracks. My wife... she says I'm making something out of nothing. She says I just look like a man who's worked outdoors his whole life. But I just... I don't see it that way.
Do you think other people actually notice the cracks and spots on your face and hands, or is it more that you're worried about what they might think?
I... I couldn't really say. I don't ask them. It just feels like they're looking, but... I don't know for a fact what's going through their heads.
Do you think your face and hands actually look as bad as you feel they do?
I don't... I don't really know how to answer that. I just know what I see when I look in the mirror. Whether it's as bad as I think... I couldn't say. It's just what I see.
When your wife or others tell you that you look fine, that your face and hands just show signs of working outdoors, do you think they're being honest with you?
I... I suppose they think they are. I don't really know. I guess they mean well, but... I just don't see what they see.
Do you think it's possible that your face and hands look less damaged than you think they do?
I suppose it could be. I just... I don't really know how to judge that. I just see what's there.
Do you think there's any possibility that your face and hands actually look normal to other people?
Maybe. I... I couldn't really say. It's hard to know what other people are looking at. I just know what's there.
Is there one particular spot, crack, or feature on your face or hands that bothers you the most?

Not just one spot, no. It's... well, it's all of it. I just can't get past how rough and worn my face and hands look. The cracks, the spots... the sagging. 

It's hard when I have to go to town. I just feel like every banker or county person is staring right at all those cracks and spots. My wife keeps saying I just look like a man who's worked outdoors, but... I don't know. I just can't get past it.
Do you think it's possible that your perception of your face and hands is not accurate?
I... I don't know. I mean, maybe? It's just hard to believe that when I look in the mirror and see it plain as day.
Is there something specific that you think is wrong with your face and hands that you wish you could change?
I don't really know. Like I was saying, it's not just one specific thing. It's... just all of it. I wouldn't even know where to start changing it. I just wish it didn't look the way it does.
Do you think your face and hands look worse to you than they do to other people?

I don't know. Maybe. My wife says they don't... she says I just look like a man who's worked outside his whole life. But... I don't know how she can say that. When I go to town, I just feel like... like the bankers or the county folks, they're all just staring right at the cracks and the spots and the sagging. It's just... I can't get past how rough and worn it all looks.
When you look at other people who have worked outdoors, do you think they have similar signs of wear on their faces and hands?
I... I guess I don't really pay much mind to other folks. I mean, maybe they do. But... I don't know. I'm not really looking at them. I just... I just see how bad mine is.
When you think about your face and hands, do you believe that others can see the flaws you're concerned about just by looking at you?

Yeah... I do. Like I was saying a minute ago, I just feel like they're staring right at it. The county folks, I mean. The spots and the sagging... it's all just right there out in the open. I know my wife says I just look like a guy who works outside, but... I just can't get past it. I feel like everyone can see how rough and worn it is.
Is there something you believe is uniquely wrong with your face and hands that you don't see in other people who have worked outdoors?

I don't know about unique... I just know what I see. Like I said, I can't get past how rough and worn they look. It's just... the cracks, the spots, the sagging. It's all I can focus on. My wife says it's just from working outside, but... when I'm around those county folks or bankers, I just feel like that's all they're looking at.
Do you think others can actually see the flaws in your face and hands that bother you, or is it something that only you notice?

Yeah... I think they see it. I mean... I feel like they do. Like I said, those county folks and bankers... I just feel like they're staring right at the cracks and spots. My wife says they don't, but... I don't know. To me, it's just... it's all right there.
Do you think your face and hands would look any different to you if nobody else ever commented on them?
I... I don't know. Nobody really comments on them anyway. It's just... I still see it when I look in the mirror. I don't think it would change what I see.
